name: parallel_contention_benchmark
declared: 24 October 2026, before any parallel live run
question: Do several live resource episodes at once on one PC change what the execution helpers achieve, through CPU contention on their wall-clock limits?
why: The bridge's helpers stop on wall-clock limits (SEARCH 36 s, canopy descent 20 s, table approach 18 s, navigation 12 s, log pickup 9 s), so contention can change successes and decision counts, not only task time. This is a methods check that decides how many episodes may run at once; it says nothing about learning.
arm: masked random baseline, frozen, no learning: resource-demo --random-baseline --condition masked --max-steps 60 --pause 0, in four chunks of five worlds with agent seeds 0 to 3 (the same chunks and seeds in every plan, so each world sees the same random stream at every slot count)
world_seeds: 30000 to 30019 (20 worlds, never used before; never used as training, validation, or test seeds)
order: Dry-run each plan first. Run 1 slot, then 4 slots, with nothing else running on the PC. Run 2 slots only if 4 slots fails the adoption rule.
measured: invalid episodes and their recorded errors
successes out of completed episodes with the Wilson 95% interval
mean task seconds per decision: mean task seconds over completed episodes divided by mean decisions
mean world startup seconds: elapsed_wall_seconds minus seconds, per completed episode
max_running_observed and each run's max_running from schedule.json, and any retired ports
report: run.cmd resource-report runs\bench-1slot runs\bench-4slots (each schedule folder stands for every run and continuation it recorded); slot counts are separate groups by construction
adoption_rule: N slots (4, or 2 if 4 fails) are adopted only if, compared with 1 slot on the same 20 worlds: (a) no episode is invalid because of the parallel setup (busy port, server startup timeout, bridge timeout); (b) successes are at least the 1-slot successes minus 2; (c) exploration_time_budget events are at most the 1-slot count plus 2; and (d) mean task seconds per decision are at most 1.25 times the 1-slot value. If 4 and 2 slots both fail, live episodes keep running one at a time.
afterwards: An adopted N is used for whole experiments only: every arm of one experiment runs with the same N, in one schedule, with interleave and evaluate_after_all_training, and the report never compares runs with different slot counts.
limits: An engineering check on 20 worlds, not a statistical test. Random choices and server timing make outcomes noisy, so the thresholds are declared tolerances. It does not show that contention is harmless for other helpers, tasks, or machines; rerun it on a new PC (for example the RTX 5080 machine) before trusting parallel runs there.
